Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the SolaraTech Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the Q&A button in the webcast console if joining online. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SolaraTech's results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Marcus Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Lena Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Sustainability Officer; Chris Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Strategy Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Marcus Hale.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. SolaraTech continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in the Q2 2024. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance. We delivered outstanding overall performance highlights and key achievements, robust revenue and earnings growth analysis, strong gross margin and operating margin trends, impressive capacity factor performance by technology across solar, wind, and storage, significant progress in storage deployment and hybrid project updates, detailed capital expenditure and operating expense management, capitalizing on significant market trends and their impact, and clear capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Elena Vasquez to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Marcus. Our financial performance in the Q2 2024 was exceptional. Revenue reached $1.45 billion, representing a 52% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $162 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $185 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into these results, let me walk you through the details that continue to reflect the structural improvements we're driving across our solar PV manufacturing, energy storage systems, and clean tech EPC operations here at SolaraTech. Our business model is vertically integrated—from silicon ingot production and TOPCon cell manufacturing to bifacial module assembly and BESS deployment—positioning us uniquely in a market shifting rapidly toward utility-scale and distributed generation amid the global energy transition.

On gross margins, we came in at 28.5% for Q2, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 25.2% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q1's 27.4%. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, now well above our long-term target of 25-27% and approaching levels seen at peers like First Solar. Key drivers include manufacturing yield and cost efficiencies: our U.S.-based Gigafactory 2 in Ohio hit 98.5% module yields on our Gen-3 TOPCon lines, up from 95% a year ago. We've fully transitioned 85% of output from PERC to n-type TOPCon cells, which deliver 22.8% average efficiency—gaining us a 1.5% cost-per-watt advantage over legacy PERC amid falling silver paste prices down 15% year-over-year. Average module costs dropped to $0.24 per watt, a 12% year-over-year decline, driven by localized wafer supply from our new Ohio polysilicon plant, benefiting from IRA Section 45X credits averaging $0.04 per watt.

Scale and fixed cost leverage also played a big role, with shipments growing 45% year-over-year to 4.2 GW, primarily utility-scale projects like the 1.2 GW Desert Sun portfolio in California. This volume absorbed fixed manufacturing overheads, contributing about 200 basis points to margin expansion. Our utilization rates are now at 92% across three factories in Ohio, Texas, and Vietnam, versus 78% last year. Product mix shift helped too: higher-margin energy storage systems, including our 5 MWh containerized BESS with LFP cells sourced via partnerships like CATL, represented 22% of revenue and delivered 35% gross margins—up from 18% mix last year. EPC services for hybrid solar-plus-storage projects, such as our 500 MW deal with NextEra in Florida, added another 150 basis points tailwind at 42% margins.

Regionally, North America, driving 55% of Q2 revenue, hit 31% gross margins, fueled by IRA incentives and domestic content bonuses—like the 10% ITC adder for U.S.-made modules. Europe, at 25% of revenue, saw 27% margins amid REPowerEU-driven demand, though tempered by €0.01 per watt Chinese dumping tariffs. APAC faced headwinds from module oversupply, with Vietnam shipments at 24% margins due to 50% capacity utilization there, but we're pivoting to export-oriented production. Looking ahead, we expect Q3 gross margins of 29-30%, with full-year 2024 at 28.5-29%, supported by further TOPCon-to-HJT ramp targeting 25% plus efficiency by Q4 and $150 million in annual COGS savings from robotic automation.

Turning to operating margins, which expanded to 12.3% in Q2—up 250 basis points year-over-year from 9.8% and 80 basis points sequentially. This brings us to our strongest in three years, outpacing Enphase's recent 10-12% range and closing the gap with pure-play manufacturers like JinkoSolar at 13-15%. SG&A as a percentage of revenue dropped to 8.2% from 9.5% year-over-year, thanks to $20 million in headcount optimization—non-production roles flat at 1,200—and AI-driven sales forecasting reducing bad debt provisions by 30%. R&D intensity held steady at 4.1% or $28 million, focused on perovskite tandem cells at 29.5% lab efficiency and virtual power plant software for our SolaraOS platform, which monetizes ESS dispatch for 2-3% incremental revenue. Other OpEx saw stock-based comp dilution ease to 1.5%, and we booked a $5 million gain from California LCFS credits on our green hydrogen pilot.

These trends underscore our Fortress North America playbook: 70% of 2024 capex, totaling $800 million, is U.S.-focused to capture $12 per watt in IRA manufacturing credits over the next decade. We're mitigating China risk via supply chain diversification—now 60% non-China components—and hedging 80% of silver exposure. Headwinds like inflation—labor up 5% year-over-year—and interest rates pressured us by about 50 basis points, but offset by pricing power: ASPs held at $0.32 per watt despite 10% global module price deflation. Forward guidance: Q3 op margins at 13-14%, FY24 at 12.5-13.5%, with 2025 potential for 15% plus as HJT scales and ESS hits 30% mix. This positions us for sustained free cash flow positivity—$250 million expected in H2—funding bolt-on M&A like our recent $100 million acquisition of a U.S. tracker firm akin to Nextracker.

Shifting to operational metrics that underpin these financials, our company-wide blended capacity factor reached 34.2% in Q2, up 180 basis points year-over-year and marking our strongest quarterly performance since the 2022 commissioning ramp of our Southwest solar fleet. This outperformance stems from advanced technology deployments, site-specific optimizations, and AI-driven forecasting integrated with our proprietary RenewaOS platform—a digital twin system extended across our hybrid assets. We've also benefited from favorable weather patterns, including above-average insolation in the U.S. Southwest and steady wind regimes in the Midwest and Texas ERCOT markets.

For solar PV, representing 42% of our 12.5 GW operational portfolio, Q2 fleet capacity factor averaged 27.8%, a 210 basis points improvement year-over-year and 90 basis points sequentially. This exceeds NREL benchmarks for fixed-tilt utility-scale PV and aligns with SEIA data for tracker-equipped systems. Key drivers included our accelerated bifacial module rollout—now 68% of new capacity—using high-efficiency TOPCon cells achieving above 22.5% module-level efficiencies. In our 800 MW Gemini Solar project in Nevada, bifacial gains coupled with Nextracker's TrueCapture single-axis trackers pushed site CF to 32.1%, up from 29.2% in 2023, thanks to back-of-module albedo enhancements. U.S. Southwest assets hit 30.4% CF with 6.2 kWh/m²/day insolation—10% above averages—while Texas reached 28.9%. Our Australian fleet averaged 26.2% amid cloud cover, but HJT retrofits target 2-3% uplift by year-end. We're prioritizing co-location with storage, like at Spring Valley hybrid where solar CF improved 4% via dispatchable clipping.

On wind, our 5.8 GW fleet delivered onshore at 37.5% CF—up 250 basis points year-over-year—and offshore at 51.2%—up 320 basis points—outperforming IRENA global averages. Onshore Midwest and Texas assets, anchored by 600 MW Rattlesnake Road in Oklahoma, averaged 39.1%, propelled by repowering 25% of pre-2015 fleet with Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines and wake steering via RenewaOS reducing losses by 3.7%. Texas ERCOT winds hit 38.8%, capturing $45 million in scarcity pricing. Offshore, our stake in 900 MW Hornsea Three delivered 52.8% CF. Initiatives include hybrid wind-solar pilots boosting blended CF to 41%.

For energy storage, our 3.2 GWh deployed averaged 28.4% equivalent capacity factor, up 15% year-over-year, with 92.1% RTE. Deployments like 850 MWh Eddy County BESS achieved 31.2% via ERCOT peaks. Our AI curtailment forecaster enables 98% accuracy. California led at 32.5%, Australia at 29.8%. We're scaling 8-hour systems co-located with 70% of new solar/wind. In aggregate, these metrics translate to 2.1 TWh of clean dispatch in Q2, 12% above guidance. FY guidance: blended CF 34.5-35.5%, with 15% year-over-year storage growth.

On revenue and earnings growth, Q2 revenue of $1.45 billion marked 52% year-over-year growth and 18% quarter-over-quarter, our ninth consecutive quarter of accelerating expansion, outpacing industry averages. H1 cumulative at $2.6 billion puts us on track for full-year $5.8-6.2 billion. Adjusted EBITDA hit $420 million at 29% margin, up from 22%, with net income $185 million or $0.72 EPS, beating consensus by 15%. Free cash flow was $280 million. Drivers include IRA benefits estimated at $150 million, data center demand, and 25% polysilicon price decline.

Segments: utility-scale solar 52% of revenue up 65% with 2.8 GWdc shipments; ESS 28% up 78% with 1.5 GWh; distributed 20% up 28%. North America 68% up 60%, Europe 22% up 35%, APAC 10% up 42%. Trends like electrification, cost compression, and technical initiatives like sodium-ion batteries support outlook: Q3 revenue $1.6-1.7 billion, FY EBITDA $1.55-1.65 billion.

Our overall performance highlights include commissioning 1.8 GW bringing fleet to 12.5 GW, EBITDA $425 million at 29.3% margins, net income $210 million or $0.78 EPS, FCF $320 million. Regional wins in U.S., Europe, APAC; R&D breakthroughs in perovskites at 32.5% efficiency, hydrogen JV. Pipeline 25 GW, 65% contracted.

On CAPEX and OPEX: Q2 CAPEX $285 million, H1 $520 million up 28%. Solar $148 million, wind $80 million, BESS $43 million, hydrogen/R&D $14 million. U.S. 70%, Europe 20%, APAC 10%. FY24 $1.1-1.2 billion. OPEX $162 million or $18 million per GW flat year-over-year, down to 22% of revenue. O&M $73 million, SG&A $49 million, R&D/other $40 million. OPEX per MWh down 15% to $8/MWh.

Significant market trends: global renewables added 510 GW in 2023, 630 GW projected 2024; solar LCOE below $30/MWh. U.S. IRA unlocked investments; Europe policy fragmentation; APAC hydrogen push. Storage doubled to 75 GWh. Our responses: $2.5 billion 2024 CAPEX, buyback.

I'll now turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our project development activities.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Elena. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 125 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring a substantial number of new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth. In Q2, we achieved record storage deployment of 450 MW / 1,800 MWh BESS, up 35% quarter-over-quarter and 120% year-over-year, bringing total to 2.3 GW / 9.2 GWh. Key projects: 200 MW / 800 MWh Rattlesnake Flats in ERCOT, two 100 MW / 400 MWh in CAISO. EBITDA margins 62%, IRR over 14%. Hybrids now 75% of pipeline at 8.2 GW, with 3.1 GW under construction. U.S. 70%, Europe growing, APAC emerging. Technically, SolStor Optimizer uplifted revenues 12%. FY24 guidance 1.8-2.0 GW storage, 4.5 GW hybrids; FY25 3.5 GW storage.

Dr. Lena Kim, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing groundbreaking technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies like perovskite tandems at 32.5% efficiency, energy storage solutions including sodium-ion and flow batteries, and smart grid technologies like SolaraOS VPP software. Our green hydrogen electrolyzer pilots are advancing, targeting 10 MW by year-end with PEM tech. We believe that these technologies will revolutionize the energy landscape.

Next, Taylor Brooks will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Dr. Kim. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions intensity by 45% year-over-year to 8 gCO2e/kWh, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management including 95% circularity targets. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability, earning an S&P Global ESG score of 85/100.

Now, Chris Patel will provide operational highlights.

Chris Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best-in-class practices in areas such as asset management with AI predictive maintenance reducing downtime 22-25%, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing heavily in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to excel, with utilization at 92% and availability over 97%.

Sophia Grant, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Sophia Grant:
Thank you, Chris. We are focused on executing our long-term strategic plan, which includes expanding our presence in key markets like U.S. Southwest and APAC, diversifying our product offerings into LDES and hydrogen, and strengthening our partnerships such as JVs with Fluence and Adani Green. We are also actively exploring new opportunities in emerging areas such as green hydrogen and carbon capture, with $2 billion dry powder for M&A.

And finally, Raj Singh, can you address our risk management strategies?

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Sophia. We have implemented robust risk management strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with our operations, including market risks like polysilicon volatility hedged at 80%, regulatory risks from tariffs and permitting, and environmental risks from climate variability and supply chain disruptions. We are continuously monitoring and evaluating our risk profile—such as interconnection queues at 3.5 years average—and taking proactive steps like domestic manufacturing and transmission partnerships to manage these risks effectively.

I'll turn it back to Marcus for closing remarks.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you all. In conclusion, SolaraTech had a truly exceptional Q2 2024. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our unwavering focus on sustainability will continue to drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, and good afternoon, team. Could you provide an update on storage deployment and hybrid project progress? Specifically, how are you progressing against your FY24 guidance amid battery supply chain dynamics and the evolving hybrid market?

Elena Vasquez:
Absolutely, Sarah. Thank you for the question. Our storage deployment and hybrid project initiatives continue to be a cornerstone of our growth strategy at SolaraTech, driving diversified revenue streams and positioning us as a leader in dispatchable clean energy. As I detailed earlier, we've reaffirmed FY24 guidance for 1.8-2.0 GW storage deployments and 4.5 GW hybrid starts, with strong progress amid stabilizing supply chains—95% contracted through 2025 with CATL and LG using LFP chemistry. Hybrids de-risk our queue and unlock premiums, contributing 45% of EBITDA by FY26.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Larson with RenewEnergy Advisors. Please go ahead.

Mike Larson:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Marcus Hale:
Great question, Mike. Competition is intensifying, but our vertically integrated model, U.S.-centric Fortress strategy, and tech leadership in TOPCon, HJT, and hybrids give us an edge. We've diversified supply chains to 60% non-China, secured backlog at premium pricing, and pursued M&A like our tracker acquisition. This allows us to maintain top-quartile ROIC at 18% while scaling faster than peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with EcoInvest Partners. Please go ahead.

Priya Patel:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Priya. Climate change poses risks like variable resource patterns, but our portfolio is resilient with geographic diversification—strong Southwest solar, Midwest/Texas wind—and AI forecasting via RenewaOS achieving 98% accuracy. We've stress-tested assets against IPCC scenarios, hedging weather via storage firming and insurance. Upside includes policy tailwinds like IRA for adaptation, keeping our risk profile low with DSCR over 1.8x.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Green Horizon Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Could you walk us through your updated capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets? Specifically, how are you thinking about execution risks amid supply chain volatility and grid interconnection delays?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. We're raising FY24 capacity addition guidance to 2.3 GWac from 2.0 GW—1.8 GWac U.S., 300 MWac Australia, 200 MWac India. FY25 4.5-5.0 GWac, scaling to 8-10 GWac annually by FY27 against our 125 GWac pipeline. Risks mitigated by 85% hedged PPAs/LOCs, Queue Jump partnerships cutting times, and 75% interconnection success rate.

Marcus Hale:
Elena, spot on. Our backlog: 3.2 GWac under construction, 18 GWac advanced, 104 GWac early-stage. U.S. 70% with IRA benefits; strategic tech like n-type IBC, M&A dry powder, and hedges position us for 50 GWac operational by 2030.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Marcus Hale for any closing remarks.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of SolaraTech. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
